title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010001-4 — Experiment Results, 1974
description: A very large (258-page) compilation held in the CIA's SRI parapsychology files, with publisher metadata pointing to Macmillan Journals (the publisher of the journal Nature) and unrelated technical content such as electron optics. title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010002-3 — Experiment Results, 1974
description: A copy of the landmark research paper 'Information Transmission Under Conditions of Sensory Shielding' by Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff of Stanford Research Institute, the work later published in Nature in 1974. It reports SRI experiments in which subjects including Uri Geller and Pat Price attempted to reproduce hidden drawings and describe remote locations under shielded, double-blind conditions. The paper is the most cited public product of the SRI program and the document that brought government-funded psychic research to mainstream scientific attention, though its controls and reporting were later sharply criticized.

title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010005-0 — Other, 1975

It relates to their long-running studies of precognition in business executives, work popularized in the 1974 book 'Executive ESP.' Retained in the SRI files as background on parallel American parapsychology research outside the SRI program itself.

title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010006-9 — Experiment Results, 1974
description: An experiment report from the Stanford Research Institute remote-viewing studies describing trials with Uri Geller and Pat Price, including drawing-reproduction tests conducted in a shielded room and remote-location descriptions such as the Rinconada Park target. The material overlaps with the data underlying the SRI Nature paper, with references to EEG monitoring and statistical scoring. It documents the primary-source experimental record behind the program's best-known published claims.

title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010007-8 — Research Report, 1973

The document illustrates early attempts to find a respectable physical theory for the alleged remote-viewing effects, rather than reporting any experiment.

title: CIA-RDP79-00999A000200010009-6 — Experiment Results, 1957

Retained as theoretical background; despite the 1957 date attached to it, it reflects the conceptual groundwork the SRI program later drew on.

It is one of many SRI session write-ups the CIA collected to assess whether remote viewing could yield usable intelligence.

Harvalik and Christopher Bird, parapsychologist Dean Radin, and U.S. Army Engineering Laboratory work at Fort Belvoir, with an eye to Soviet/East Bloc interest in the phenomenon. The document reflects the program's effort to ground anomalous-detection claims in measurable mechanisms.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300030001-7 — Experiment Results, 1984
description: A 16-page report under SRI Project 6600 (c. 1984), part of Edwin May's Cognitive Sciences work, that takes a more analytical and simulation-oriented approach to remote viewing and detection, again referencing Harvalik, Christopher Bird, and Dean Radin. It appears to model search/detection over a continuum and assess facility-level targeting, with attention to Soviet/East Bloc activity. The document exemplifies the program's shift toward quantitative methodology and applied targeting analysis.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300040001-6 — Experiment Results, 1985
description: An unclassified 15-page report (c. 1985) from SRI's program documenting an examination of claimed photon-production and psychokinesis effects associated with paranormal/qigong practitioners in the People's Republic of China, with technical results from photomultiplier-tube measurements. It describes the photon-detection equipment and instrumentation used to test for physical signatures, referencing reporting such as National Geographic coverage from China. The document reflects SRI's interest in evaluating Chinese 'exceptional function' research using laboratory physics methods.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300050001-5 — Psychokinesis, 1982
description: A paper on psychokinesis (mental influence on physical systems) associated with SRI International's psychoenergetics work and co-authored by Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ. It reviews and analyzes experiments in which subjects attempt to bias random number generators (RNGs) and other devices by intention, drawing on the parapsychology literature including the Journal of Parapsychology and the Journal of the American Society for Psychical Research. It is part of the program's effort to document claimed mind-matter interaction effects, including any apparent independence from distance.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300060001-4 — Experiment Results, 1981
description: An SRI International experiment report on remote viewing that compares different targeting modes, including beacon (an outbound person at the site) versus coordinate or other cued techniques. It presents the protocol, the resulting remote-viewing data, caveats, and conclusions about how the targeting method affects performance. The document reflects the program's continuing work to refine task design and identify the most reliable approach for tasking viewers.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300070001-3 — Experiment Results (In the past, 1987)
description: An SRI International report on a remote-influence experiment carried out with C. M. Pleass of the University of Delaware's College of Marine Studies, testing whether subjects could mentally affect a biological or physical system. It includes Monte Carlo calculations and variance analysis used to assess statistical significance, and was prepared under the program's standard government client arrangement (contracting officer Peter J. McNelis). It is notable as one of the program's forays into anomalous mind-matter interaction beyond perceptual remote viewing.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300080001-2 — Research Report, 1983
description: An unclassified SRI International research report, authored by Harold Puthoff, Russell Targ, and Edwin C. May, that surveys and organizes the international parapsychology literature using a keyword-based classification system. It catalogs research on remote sensing, remote action, reliability and screening, and theories and models, drawing on work from the U.S. and numerous countries including England, the Netherlands, West Germany, and Israel. The report served as a literature-survey and indexing tool to map the state of psychoenergetic research worldwide.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300090001-1 — Experiment Results, 1987
description: An SRI International experiment report co-authored with William W. Braud of the Mind Science Foundation (San Antonio) and statistician Jessica Utts, prepared under contracting officer Peter J. McNelis. It documents experiments in anomalous mental influence or perception, with Utts providing the statistical analysis and methodology. The report is part of the program's mid-1980s effort to test and rigorously evaluate mind-matter and remote-perception effects with outside collaborators.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300100001-9 — Experiment Results (MILESTONE CHART , 1987)
description: A lengthy unclassified SRI International report organized around a project milestone chart, summarizing remote-viewing experiments, program resources, and progress for the contract year. It includes RV transcripts and analysis of trials against targets described in urban and geographic terms (e.g., open-city and river scenes) and discusses the problem of noisy data. The document functions as a combined progress and results report for the Cognitive Sciences Program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300110001-8 — Experiment Results, 1986
description: An unclassified 1986 SRI International report, "A Suggested Remote Viewing Training Procedure," prepared by Gary Langford (Consultants International) and SRI. It compiles the subjective experiences and perceptual stages reported during remote viewing and proposes a structured method intended to develop and improve viewer reliability. It is notable as one of the program's attempts to turn remote viewing into a trainable, teachable procedure rather than a talent confined to a few gifted subjects.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300130001-6 — Experiment Results, 1992
description: A short report or correspondence concerning EEG-based experiments by Russian researchers Yuri S. Dolin, Victor I. Dymov, and Nicolai N. Khatchenkov, including Fourier analysis of brain activity and control conditions. The fragmentary Cyrillic-laced text and variance figures suggest a translated or summarized account of Soviet/Russian psychophysiological work relevant to the program's interest in foreign psychoenergetic research. Its brevity (about three pages) indicates a summary or data note rather than a full study.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300150001-4 — Experiment Results, 1988
description: An SRI International experiment report on remote viewing in which viewers attempted to describe a target site, apparently involving a wind-power electric generator farm (such as Altamont Pass) and naval or other installations. It presents the RV responses, the analytical scoring of merit, and the experimental protocol. The document is one of the program's many trial reports assessing how accurately viewers could perceive real-world technical and geographic targets.

title:
CIA-RDP96-00787R000300160001-3 — Experiment Results (By

Ralph J, 1986)
description: A brief SRI International report involving Ralph J. Kiernan of Stanford Medical School and psychologist John Gittinger, prepared under contracting officer Peter J. McNelis. It appears to concern neuropsychological assessment of remote-viewer subjects, referencing cognitive measures such as the Digit Symbol and maze tests used to characterize or screen participants. The work reflects the program's interest in identifying psychological and cognitive correlates of remote-viewing ability.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300170001-2 — Experiment Results, 1989
description: A 1989 SRI International report authored by Edwin C. May, Thane J. Frivold, and statistician Jessica M. Utts, with Beverly Humphrey and Virginia Trask, prepared for the program's government client. It addresses methodological and analytical questions in anomalous cognition, including target-pool design, causal processes, and statistical effect-size calculations, and references prior work such as Honorton's ganzfeld studies. The report is part of the Cognitive Sciences Program's late-1980s effort to put remote-viewing evaluation on a rigorous statistical footing.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300180001-1 — Experiment Results, 1989
description: A 1989 SRI International report prepared by Nevin D. Lantz (a consultant based in Jefferson, N.C.) for the Cognitive Sciences Program. It documents a remote-viewing experiment and its protocols, with discussion touching on viewer memory effects (hypermnesia) and comparison to outside work such as Honorton's. The roughly nine-page report records the method and results of a specific RV trial series in the program's standard final-report format.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300200001-8 — Experiment Results, 1984
description: An unclassified 1984 SRI International report (Project 6600) on remote-viewing learning that incorporates a Mobius Society questionnaire and a baseline/confirmation data-acquisition design, with consultant Nevin Lantz and psychologist John Gittinger. It examines whether RV performance can be enhanced and includes material on neurolinguistic programming (NLP) as a candidate training aid. The document reflects the program's mid-1980s search for methods to improve and train remote-viewing ability.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300280001-0 — Experiment Results, 1976
description: A research paper from the SRI psychoenergetics group (referencing Puthoff and Targ and later Cognitive Sciences Laboratory staff including Edwin C. May and Jessica Utts) reviewing remote-viewing and related psi experiments and their statistical evaluation. It engages the broader parapsychology literature and figures such as Charles Honorton, citing the Journal of Parapsychology and the Society for Psychical Research. The piece situates SRI's findings within the wider field of published psi replications and critiques.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300290001-9 — Experiment Results, 1989
description: "An Application Oriented Remote Viewing Experiment," a 1989 SRI International final report by Edwin C. May for the Cognitive Sciences Program. It documents an extended remote-viewing trial using an experienced viewer against an operational-style target and tests the analytical technique used to score the results. The report aimed to demonstrate the practical potential of remote viewing and to assess how broadly the scoring methodology could be applied.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000300300001-7 — Experiment Results, 1987
description: A large 1987 SRI International final report ("Objective H") prepared with Julian Isaacs of John F. Kennedy University, investigating psychokinesis or anomalous perturbation of physical systems. It describes modifications to the apparatus and experimental participants, with instrumentation references such as a Scientific-Atlanta spectrum analyzer, and presents the study's methods and results across more than sixty pages. The report is among the program's most substantial mind-matter interaction studies, conducted with an outside parapsychology specialist.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400010010-8 — Research Report, 1979
description: A Russian-language document held in the program's files, heavily garbled in OCR but apparently concerning psychotherapy and psychophysiology rather than a U.S. SRI study. Filed under the CIA-RDP96-00787R series, it appears to be foreign-source material collected for the program's interest in Soviet/Russian work on the mind and altered states. Its content cannot be reconstructed in detail from the available metadata, so this synopsis is necessarily tentative.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400010012-6 — Telepathy, 1974
description: A five-page translated extract of Soviet parapsychology writing, part of the foreign-literature collection the CIA assembled while monitoring USSR work on telepathy. It cites figures such as physiologist L.L. Vasiliev, references Soviet reference works like Sovetskaya Entsiklopediya, and discusses telepathic and 'mysterious phenomena of the human mind' research centered in Leningrad and Moscow. The material reflects the CIA's effort to gauge Soviet interest in mental suggestion at a distance, a recurring driver of the agency's own psychic-research funding.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400010036-0 — Research Report, 1966
description: A lengthy 22-page research report from 1966 surveying Soviet and Eastern-bloc parapsychology, again drawing heavily on the work of Leningrad physiologist L.L. Vasiliev. It discusses telepathy and related 'biological communication' experiments, with references to research in the USSR, Czechoslovakia and India. The document is one of many in this collection through which the CIA tracked the scope and seriousness of Soviet psychic research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400020014-3 — Telepathy, 1964
description: A short translated compilation of Soviet sources on telepathy and 'biological communication,' assembled circa 1964 as part of the agency's monitoring of USSR parapsychology. It quotes Soviet encyclopedias and press (Sovetskaya Entsiklopediya, Nedelya, Trud, Moskovskiy Komsomolets) and names researchers including Vasiliev and Zinchenko. The piece illustrates how the CIA used open Soviet publications to assess official interest in mental suggestion and the 'phenomena of the human mind.'

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400030015-1 — Experiment Results, 1969
description: A heavily OCR-degraded five-page item filed as experiment results, circa 1969, concerning psychical research in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe. Despite garbled text, it appears to summarize experimental work and named researchers in the Soviet/Eastern European parapsychology scene the CIA was tracking. The poor scan quality leaves specific findings unclear, but it fits the collection's pattern of foreign psychic-research intelligence.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400030058-4 — Research Report, 1996
description: A short research report associated with American parapsychologist Douglas Dean of the Newark College of Engineering, discussing Soviet bioenergetics work including Kirlian photography and the research of V.M. Inyushin. It touches on claims about energy fields, healing and the perceived gap between Soviet and U.S. investment in such research. The piece reflects the CIA's interest in Western scientists' assessments of Soviet psychic and bioenergy claims.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400040007-9 — Experiment Results, 1972
description: A brief two-page document filed as experiment results, with almost no usable extracted metadata beyond release stamps and references to a 'Hard Drug Disruption Process' and research assistance. The garbled text makes its precise subject uncertain, though it appears to be a short administrative or research note within the agency's parapsychology and behavioral-research files. Specific content cannot be reliably reconstructed from the available data.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400040016-9 — Correspondence, 1967
description: A one-page piece of correspondence (about 430 words) from 1967, with a Baltimore connection and a sanitized sender. With names redacted and little extractable content, it appears to be routine administrative or referral correspondence within the agency's parapsychology-related file series. The thin metadata does not support identifying its specific subject.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400040022-2 — Research Report, 1964
description: An 18-page academic bibliographic and theoretical paper by Arnold E. Dahlke on social exchange theory and group behavior, citing social psychologists such as Thibaut, Kelley, Secord, Backman and Goffman. Rather than psychic research, it deals with mainstream small-group social psychology, status, and group maintenance. Its presence in the file reflects the agency's broad collection of behavioral-science literature alongside its parapsychology holdings.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400040024-0 — Other, 1968
description: A three-page 1968 item concerning the standing of parapsychology within organized science, naming AAAS figures and referencing the American Association for the Advancement of Science and its Board of Directors. It bears on the debate over the Parapsychological Association's bid for scientific legitimacy, which culminated in the PA's 1969 AAAS affiliation. The document shows the agency following the field's struggle for institutional acceptance.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400040026-8 — Research Report, 1969
description: A one-page 1969 note tied to dream-telepathy research, referencing the Maimonides Dream Laboratory, the Society for Psychical Research, the American Psychological Association, and figures such as Gardner Murphy. It appears to be a brief report or notice on personnel and activity in the experimental dream-ESP community centered in New York. The item reflects CIA awareness of U.S. academic parapsychology, including the EEG/REM dream studies of Ullman and Krippner.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400060006-8 — Correspondence, 1966
description: A very short (about 68-word) one-page piece of 1966 correspondence with a sanitized sender. With essentially no extractable content, it appears to be a brief routing slip or cover note within the agency's parapsychology file series. The metadata is too thin to determine its specific subject.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400060007-7 — Correspondence, 1966
description: A brief one-page 1966 item connected to the American Society for Psychical Research and the Parapsychological Association, apparently a membership or annual-dues notice. It documents the agency's contact with, or monitoring of, established U.S. psychical-research organizations in New York. The content is administrative rather than experimental.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070005-8 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A four-page 1973 item filed as experiment results, written in an informal letter style ('Dear Bart,' 'Russ et al') referencing SRI. The 'Russ' and SRI cues point to the Stanford Research Institute team of Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff, then conducting the agency-funded psychic experiments of that period. It appears to be working correspondence relaying experimental progress, though OCR damage obscures the specific results.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070010-2 — Research Report, 1973
description: A one-page 1973 item about Uri Geller, referencing Hebrew University and TIME magazine. It dates to the year of Geller's tests at Stanford Research Institute with Targ and Puthoff and of TIME's skeptical coverage of those claims. The note appears to be a brief press or background clipping the agency collected while weighing Geller's reported abilities.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070016-6 — Other, 1973
description: A one-page 1973 ORD item (routed through C/IP&A/ORD) on Rosemary Brown, the English medium who claimed dead composers such as Liszt, Bach and Beethoven dictated music to her. It also invokes names like Einstein and Joan of Arc in connection with such posthumous-communication claims and a William Morrow book. The document reflects the Office of Research and Development's interest in surveying notable paranormal claimants of the day.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070017-5 — Historical, 1967
description: A one-page 1967 item filed as historical, touching on noted intellectual figures including Lord Russell and Einstein and the conductor Donald Tovey, apparently in the context of claims about creativity, genius, or posthumous artistic communication. The fragmentary extraction leaves its exact argument unclear, but it sits among the agency's background readings on parapsychology and exceptional human ability.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070019-3 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A one-page 1973 'Paranormal Research Questionnaire' associated with the Office of Research and Development (DDS&T/ORD) and the subject Ingo Swann, listing physiological monitoring such as EEG and ECG. It dates to the early SRI-era work in which Swann was a principal psychic subject. The form appears to gather baseline data on test subjects, reflecting the agency's effort to study remote viewing and related abilities under controlled conditions.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070020-1 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A short SECRET internal memo from the CIA's early 1973 review of Stanford Research Institute (SRI) parapsychology work, referencing Dr. Harold Puthoff and the Agency's Technical Services Division (TSD) and Office of Research and Development (ORD). It touches on the SRI experiments with Uri Geller and Ingo Swann and the involvement of an SRI representative in Washington. The page is one fragment of the cluster of memoranda through which CIA components weighed whether to continue supporting the SRI program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070022-9 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A brief 1973 CIA memorandum tied to the Agency's assessment of the SRI psychic research, naming George Lawrence and referencing Geller, Swann, SRI and ARPA. Lawrence was an ARPA scientist among the skeptical observers of the Geller demonstrations, and the note appears to weigh the credibility of Geller (described in this era's documents as an Israeli 'magician') against the views of outside agencies. It is one of several short evaluative records from the program's formative period.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070024-7 — Research Report, 2000
description: A research-report page whose text is heavily degraded by OCR, leaving its specific content unreadable from the metadata alone. It belongs to the CIA/SRI parapsychology file series (RDP96-00787R) released through the FOIA Reading Room, the body of records documenting the Agency's 1970s remote-viewing and psychic research. Beyond its place in that collection, no reliable substance can be recovered for this particular item.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070025-6 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A multi-page 1973 CIA staff paper reviewing the SRI psychic research program, organized around headings such as past and present project activity, future intentions, and possible ORD involvement and contribution. It discusses the work with subjects including Swann, references TSD's earlier role, figures such as Lawrence and Kress, and physiological measures like EEG. The document is a substantive internal assessment used to decide the Agency's continued posture toward SRI's paranormal research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070029-2 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A January 1973 CIA memorandum from C/IP&A/ORD reporting on a briefing by Stanford Research Institute in which Dr. Russell Targ and Dr. Harold Puthoff showed a film of their experiments with Uri Geller, described as an Israeli magician with claimed ESP. It notes that the SRI work was supported by Edgar Mitchell's foundation and the Mind Science Institute of Los Angeles (associated with Dr. Andrija Puharich), that ARPA's George Lawrence was among the observers, and that testing had focused on behavioral tasks rather than examination of Geller himself apart from a cursory EEG. The memo is a key record of how SRI's Geller work was first presented to and debated within the Agency.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070030-0 — Research Report, 1953
description: A brief research-report page from the CIA/SRI parapsychology file series, naming SRI, TSD, ARPA, NSA and the National Science Foundation (NSF). It appears to discuss potential funding or interagency interest in the SRI psychic research, situating the program among the government bodies that might sponsor or scrutinize it. The catalogued year (1953) is almost certainly an OCR artifact; the document fits the early-1970s context of the surrounding records.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400070031-9 — Research Report, 2000
description: A longer (roughly eight-page) CIA assessment, dated to January 1973, of the SRI parapsychology effort and its principal subjects Ingo Swann and Uri Geller, with reference to Dr. Andrija (Henry) Puharich and Captain Edgar Mitchell. Structured around themes such as options, control, predictability and motivation, it weighs the scientific and operational value of the work for the Agency, involving OSI and the office of the Deputy Director for Science and Technology. It is one of the more developed internal evaluations from the program's early period.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400080004-8 — Research Report, 1973
description: A 1973 research-related record concerning instrumentation and biofield measurement, naming Dr. W. Ross Adey of UCLA's Life Sciences, the firm Develco, and Robert P. Gow of the CIA. It reflects the Agency's interest in magnetometer/gradiometer equipment (from Develco) and Adey's electromagnetic and brain-research expertise as applied to the SRI psychoenergetics work. The document is part of the technical and procurement correspondence supporting that research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400080005-7 — Research Report, 1973
description: A 1973 document, partly an address/contact record, linking the University of California (Department of Anatomy, associated with Ross Adey) and the firm Develco of Mountain View, California, with references to Robert P. Gow and to the Josephson effect. It relates to the magnetometer and biofield-measurement instrumentation the CIA was arranging in support of the SRI parapsychology program. The page documents the people and organizations involved rather than experimental results.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400080009-3 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A 1973 page outlining proposed lines of inquiry into psychic phenomena, with headings for a basic-research aspect and psychological testing and references to physiological measures such as GSR (galvanic skin response), AEP, CNV and the central nervous system. It involves the Office of Technical Service (OTS) and reads as planning or methodology for studying the bodily correlates of claimed paranormal ability. The specific findings are not recoverable from the fragmentary text.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100001-8 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: An SRI/paranormal trip report from 1973 documenting a visit involving Messrs. Cox and Puthoff and referencing Uri Geller, Ingo Swann, Hugh Crane of SRI, ORD and NASA. It records observations and discussions from the CIA's on-site contact with the SRI psychic research rather than a formal experiment. The report is part of the field documentation through which Agency officers tracked progress at SRI.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100002-7 — Administrative, 1973
description: A brief 1973 administrative record on Stanford Research Institute (Menlo Park) letterhead relating to the CIA-sponsored work with Uri Geller and Dr. Harold Puthoff. The legible content is largely routine, including the institute's cable/telex identifier (STANRES) and release markings. It functions as housekeeping correspondence within the SRI parapsychology contract rather than a substantive report.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100003-6 — Correspondence, 1976
description: A short 1976 letter on Stanford Research Institute (Menlo Park) letterhead, signed by Barbara J. Ripple, a senior systems person in SRI's Technology Applications Department, and referencing Philip Whalen and the Office of Management and Budget in Washington. It appears to be administrative or contractual correspondence connected to the SRI program. Its brevity and routine nature limit what can be said about its specific purpose.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100005-4 — Experiment Results, 1972
description: A 1972 SRI (Menlo Park) document describing early work with Ingo Swann, including his background with parapsychologist Gertrude Schmeidler at City College of New York and the experiments run with Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff. It references the now-famous test in which Swann reportedly affected a shielded magnetometer near Dr. Arthur Hebard's apparatus in the Varian Physics building at Stanford, and names figures such as Martin Lee. The record captures the foundational period when SRI's psychoenergetics research with Swann was just beginning.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100007-2 — Experiment Results, 1974
description: A short UNCLASSIFIED 1974 record from the SRI parapsychology file naming Harold Puthoff, Russell Targ, Ingo Swann and Uri Geller, and referencing EEG measurement along with address/phone contact fields. It appears to be a brief informational or contact-style note tied to the SRI program's principal researchers and subjects. The legible content is limited and contains no detailed experimental results.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100009-0 — Correspondence, 1973
description: A 1973 memorandum, badly degraded by OCR, that concerns the Stanford Research Institute work and references a biofield-measurement project, Uri Geller, and the CIA's Office of Research and Development (ORD). It reads as correspondence relating to the funding or status of an SRI experimental effort. Because the text is so garbled, only the general subject can be stated with confidence.

title:
CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100010-8 — Research Report (Officer responsible
for monitoring the validation effort, 1973)
description: A SECRET 1973 memorandum from the Office of Research and Development concerning the officer responsible for monitoring the validation effort on the SRI parapsychology research, with subjects Ingo Swann and Uri Geller. It addresses oversight of the Stanford Research Institute work and coordination with TSD and the DD/O, reflecting the Agency's effort to manage and verify the SRI experiments. The document is part of the internal record establishing how the program was supervised.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100011-7 — Administrative, 1974
description: An administrative record from the early CIA-sponsored SRI parapsychology program, apparently dating from around 1974. The single page references the SRI 'paranormal project,' its government sponsor, data-control handling, and CIA official John McMahon, who oversaw aspects of the Agency's funding of the work. It is a housekeeping document rather than a research report, reflecting the bureaucratic management of the SRI psychic-research contract in its early years.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100012-6 — Research Report, 1972
description: A research report from roughly 1972 concerning artist and psychic Ingo Swann and his work with the American Society for Psychical Research (ASPR) in New York. It recounts Swann's out-of-body and ESP experiments under Karlis Osis, alongside figures such as Gertrude Schmeidler and Edgar Mitchell, and touches on EEG monitoring and out-of-body experience (OOBE) testing. The material documents the New York parapsychology milieu from which Swann moved to SRI, where his ideas helped launch the remote-viewing program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100013-5 — Research Report, 1959
description: A short item, dated by the record to about 1959, that the CIA collected as background on parapsychology research. It appears to be a piece of correspondence or notice involving a company president (Robert P. Gow) and references to organizations such as DEVELCO and to writer Arthur Koestler. The page is thin and largely administrative; it forms part of the broader file of outside psychic-research material gathered to support the Agency's interest in the field.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100014-4 — Experiment Results, 1958
description: A lengthy (25-page) experiment report associated with New Zealand psychologist Gordon L. Mangan and the Parapsychology Foundation, dating from about 1958. It presents ESP testing work, apparently using questionnaires and intelligence/mental-ability measures with experimental subjects. Collected by the CIA as part of its survey of established parapsychology literature, it reflects the academic ESP research that predated and informed the later SRI program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100015-3 — Experiment Results, 1965
description: An unclassified copy of K. Ramakrishna Rao's monograph 'Experimental Parapsychology: A Review and Interpretation' (Charles C. Thomas, Springfield, Ill., 1966), retained in the CIA file as reference literature. The 23-page extract reviews and interprets a large body of ESP and psi experimentation, including methodology and the sender/receiver paradigm. It is a scholarly survey rather than original Agency research, gathered to ground the program in the existing scientific record.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100016-2 — Correspondence, 1973
description: A brief 1973 piece of correspondence on Stanford Research Institute (Menlo Park) letterhead concerning psychic Uri Geller. The short note references enclosed material and a Holiday Inn, consistent with logistics around Geller's testing at SRI by Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ. It is a routine administrative communication documenting the handling of the Geller experiments during the CIA-funded SRI effort.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100017-1 — Experiment Results, 2004
description: An experiment-related report tied to the early SRI work of Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ with Ingo Swann and Uri Geller, the file copy bearing a later (circa 2004) release marking. It references the New York ASPR circle—Gertrude Schmeidler and Karlis Osis at City College—and physics apparatus such as a SQUID magnetometer used to test psychokinetic effects. The document connects Swann's magnetometer demonstrations to the founding rationale for SRI's psychic-research program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100020-7 — Experiment Results, 1951
description: A research paper (circa early 1970s, with cited literature back to 1951) from J. B. Rhine's Institute for Parapsychology at Durham, N.C., involving W. J. Levy and colleagues including R. L. Morris and Louisa E. Rhine. It reports animal-psi experiments—precognition or psychokinesis tests using laboratory rodents such as Meriones gerbils—published in the Journal of Parapsychology. The CIA retained it as scientific background; notably, Levy was later exposed in 1974 for falsifying such animal-psi data.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100021-6 — Experiment Results, 1971
description: An experiment report from the Institute for Parapsychology and the Medical College of Georgia (circa 1971) credited to W. J. Levy with collaborators including J. B. Rhine and R. L. Morris. It describes animal-psi studies—precognition or PK tests on gerbils (Meriones) and other rodents—of the kind associated with the McDougall Award and published in the Journal of Parapsychology. Kept by the CIA as reference material, this line of Levy's work was central to the 1974 fraud scandal in which he admitted falsifying results.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100022-5 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: An experiment-results document from about 1973 relating to ESP and psi testing, with ties to Edgar D. Mitchell and references to the Xerox Corporation and researchers in Ohio and Ontario, Canada. It records subject testing procedures and appears connected to the wave of corporate- and Mitchell-linked psychic research of the period, including interest in Uri Geller. The CIA collected it as part of its monitoring of contemporary parapsychology activity.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000400100023-4 — Research Report, 1973
description: A 1973 research report or news/press item concerning Uri Geller's testing at Stanford Research Institute in Menlo Park by Russell Targ and Harold Puthoff, the 'think tank' where the work took place. It discusses telepathy demonstrations and includes university (Michigan) figures observing or commenting on the experiments. The piece documents the early public and scientific attention to the SRI Geller investigations that the CIA was tracking.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500020001-6 — Experiment Results, 1976
description: A substantial (47-page) SRI research report from about 1976 by Harold E. Puthoff and Russell Targ of the Electronics and Bioengineering Laboratory, Stanford Research Institute, Menlo Park. It presents remote-viewing experiments—including work on signal enhancement and trials with both gifted subjects (Pat Price, Hella Hammid, Ingo Swann) and unselected subjects—with distant geographic targets such as sites in Costa Rica, Colombia, and San Andres. This is core SRI documentation of the perceptual-channel remote-viewing research that anchored the CIA-funded program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030001-5 — Research Report, 1976
description: A report compiled by Scott Hill (circa 1976) summarizing Soviet and European bioenergetics research drawn from the German esoteric-science magazine 'Esotera.' This installment focuses on the work of A. G. Gurvich on mitogenetic radiation and on the Leningrad Brain Research Institute and L. L. Vassiliev's telepathy research, citing a Congress on frontier sciences. It is one of a series translating and digesting Eastern-bloc parapsychology and biophysics literature for U.S. intelligence interest.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030002-4 — Experiment Results, 1976
description: Another Scott Hill summary (circa 1976) of 'Esotera' coverage of Soviet bioenergetics and bioinformation research, centered on Kazakhstan (Alma-Ata) and figures such as V. Inyushin and Norwegian researcher Wilhelm Schjelderup. It touches on the Cybernetics Division work and West German aerospace firm Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm, reflecting the Congress on frontier sciences. The piece forms part of Hill's running digest of Eastern-bloc psi and 'bioplasma' studies gathered as foreign-research intelligence.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030003-3 — Other, 1976
description: A Scott Hill report (circa 1976) drawing on the German magazine 'Esotera' and a Congress on Frontier Sciences (Copenhagen/Alma-Ata) to survey Soviet and European biophoton and cell-radiation research. It highlights the Gurvich–Kaznacheyev line of work on cellular ('ten million cells per second') ultraviolet emission and intercellular communication, alongside biophysicist Fritz-Albert Popp of Marburg University. Categorized as 'other,' it continues Hill's series digesting frontier bioenergetics for the program's foreign-research file.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030004-2 — Experiment Results, 1976
description: A Scott Hill report (circa 1976) summarizing 'Esotera' material on Soviet bioenergetics and parapsychology centered on the Kazakh SSR (Alma-Ata), the Leningrad Brain Research Institute, and L. L. Vassiliev's legacy. It discusses cell-radiation and biophoton work associated with Gurvich and Fritz-Albert Popp and frames it within Soviet ideological context (Marxism-Leninism). The installment is part of Hill's ongoing digest of Eastern-bloc psi and biophysics research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030005-1 — Research Report, 1977
description: A Scott Hill report (circa 1977) drawn from 'Esotera' on healing, autogenic training, and altered-state research, referencing the Alma-Ata parapsychology conference and Soviet investigators such as A. S. Romen. It connects Western autogenic methods (Johannes Schultz), yoga and figures like Swami Rama, and historical roots back to Mesmer with Soviet clinical work. The piece rounds out Hill's series translating Eastern-bloc and comparative parapsychology and self-regulation research for the program.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500030006-0 — Research Report, 1977
description: A research report, likely a translated commentary on Soviet attitudes toward parapsychology, gathered by the CIA as part of its monitoring of Eastern-bloc psychic research. It centers on prominent Moscow psychologists V.P. Zinchenko, A.N. Leontiev, B.F. Lomov, and A.R. Luria, whose skeptical 1973 article 'Parapsychology: Fiction or Reality?' framed the official Soviet debate, and references the popular Western account of Soviet psi work by Ostrander and Schroeder. It illustrates the CIA's effort to gauge how seriously Soviet science establishment figures took claims of telepathy and 'cryptesthesia.'

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500050001-3 — Research Report, 2000
description: A lengthy translated research report drawn from Soviet/Russian-language source material and collected in the CIA's parapsychology files. Its subject matter is more historical-philological than psychic, ranging across Cossack and classical themes (Aeneas, Troy, Mycenae, Crete, Schliemann, the linguist John Chadwick) under a title rendered as 'On Ethnic Immortality.' The piece appears to be background intelligence translation rather than an experimental study, and its connection to remote-viewing work is peripheral.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500060001-2 — Experiment Results, 1977
description: A large compilation of experiment and survey material associated with Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ of Stanford Research Institute (Menlo Park), the principals of the SRI psychic-research program funded in part by the CIA. The collection touches on SRI's investigation of Soviet psychical research and involves outside figures including AiResearch Manufacturing personnel and apparently astronaut Edgar Mitchell. It documents the breadth of SRI's early- to mid-1970s effort to assess and replicate purported psychic phenomena for U.S. intelligence sponsors.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500070001-1 — Experiment Results, 1977
description: A set of experiment-related materials in the SRI psychic-research files, linking Harold Puthoff's Stanford Research Institute work to the parallel program of Robert G. Jahn, the Princeton engineering dean who would found the Princeton Engineering Anomalies Research (PEAR) laboratory. It appears to include Princeton coverage (a 'PAW'/Princeton Alumni Weekly-style report) of Jahn's interest in psychokinesis and remote viewing. The document reflects the cross-pollination between SRI's remote-viewing experiments and emerging academic anomalies research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500070002-0 — Experiment Results, 1978
description: Experiment documentation from the Stanford Research Institute remote-viewing program, attributed to Harold E. Puthoff, Russell Targ, and Edwin C. May. It addresses methodological questions such as the role of feedback in remote viewing and considers Soviet ELF (extremely low frequency) and jamming hypotheses, citing Soviet researchers L. Vasiliev and I. Kogan. The report is characteristic of SRI's late-1970s efforts to refine remote-viewing protocols and to weigh proposed physical mechanisms for the claimed effect.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500070003-9 — Correspondence, 2000
description: A very short piece of correspondence (about 186 words on a single page) held in the SRI psychic-research files. The names and content are too garbled in the available metadata to identify the sender, recipient, or subject with confidence. It appears to be a routine cover note or brief letter accompanying other program material rather than a substantive report.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500080001-0 — Experiment Results, 1976
description: An English translation of the Soviet monograph 'Biostimulation Through Laser Radiation and Bioplasma' by V.M. Inyushin and P.R. Chekerov of Kazakh State University in Alma-Ata, rendered by Scott Hill and T.D. Ghoshal for the Danish Society for Psychical Research and collected in the CIA's parapsychology files. The work elaborates Inyushin's controversial 'bioplasma' concept and its supposed interaction with laser light, drawing on earlier ideas such as Gurvich's mitogenetic radiation. It exemplifies the unconventional Soviet biophysics the CIA tracked alongside Kirlian-photography research.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090001-9 — Other, 1967
description: A short unclassified item (two pages, 1967) in the CIA's Soviet parapsychology collection concerning Kirlian-effect and 'bioplasma' research. It names S.T. Kirlian (originator of high-voltage corona-discharge photography), V.M. Inyushin of Kazakh State University in Alma-Ata, and associated medical researchers at the Kuban Medical Institute. The piece records early Soviet biophysics claims about a luminous 'bioplasma' surrounding living tissue, part of the body of work the CIA monitored for possible intelligence relevance.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090002-8 — Experiment Results, 1974
description: A translated paper, attributed to L. Vilenskaya and titled in the metadata as concerning 'luminescence phantoms,' collected among the CIA's Soviet/Eastern-bloc Kirlian-photography materials. It references the Kirlians (Semyon and Valentina), biophysicist Viktor Adamenko and V.M. Inyushin, alongside Western parapsychologists Thelma Moss, Stanley Krippner, and others, and surveys the international spread of Kirlian and bioplasma research. The report reflects 1970s interest in whether corona-discharge images captured a genuine biological field or merely electrical artifacts.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090003-7 — Research Report, 1974
description: A brief unclassified research note (one page, about 349 words, 1974) in the CIA's Kirlian-photography file. It concerns Viktor Adamenko and the Kirlian husband-and-wife team (Semyon Davidovich and Valentina Khrisanfovna Kirlian) and an associate of a Soviet Academy of Medical Sciences research institute. The fragment appears to be a short descriptive or caption-bearing item documenting Soviet corona-discharge photography work rather than a full study.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090004-6 — Remote Viewing, 1973
description: A translated conference paper from the international Congress of Psychotronic Research (Prague), authored by Soviet biophysicist Viktor G. Adamenko and dealing with 'biological electrodynamics' and psychoenergetics. It frames Kirlian-type phenomena and bioelectric effects in terms of classical electrical concepts (invoking Galvani, Coulomb, Ohm), reflecting Adamenko's interpretation of corona discharge as cold electron emission. The item is part of the CIA's collection of Soviet and East European psychotronics literature.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090005-5 — Experiment Results, 1973
description: A short unclassified paper (one page, 1973) presented at the Congress of Psychotronic Research in Prague, concerning 'the luminescence pattern' in Kirlian photography. It is associated with Soviet researchers Valerii A. Doktorovich, Viktor G. Adamenko, and Semyon D. Kirlian, working out of Simferopol/Crimea, and appears in a Journal of Paraphysics-style citation. The note documents Soviet attempts to characterize the corona-discharge glow recorded in high-voltage photography.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090006-4 — Experiment Results, 1971
description: A translated Soviet experimental paper (about three pages, 1971) in the CIA's unconventional-biophysics file, drawn from sources such as the Bulletin of Experimental Biology. Authored by researchers including R.L. Vilenskaya, A.Z. Smolyanskaya, and M.B. Golant, it reports on the biological effects of millimeter-wave (microwave) radiation, work conducted under the Soviet Academy of Medical Sciences and electronics-industry institutes. It reflects CIA interest in Soviet research at the boundary of microwave bioeffects and claimed bioplasma phenomena.

title: CIA-RDP96-00787R000500090007-3 — Experiment Results, 1969
description: A translated Soviet research item (about five pages, 1969) in the CIA's Kirlian-photography collection, centering on the Kirlian high-voltage photographic method (S.D. Kirlian) and its clinical/diagnostic use, with references tied to the Krasnodar hospital and Leningrad University. It surveys corona-discharge imaging of living tissue and notes related work in Japan and elsewhere. The document is part of the broader file documenting Soviet bioplasma and Kirlian-effect claims that U.S. intelligence sought to assess.
